Will there be someone who assumes a sacred title, or will any mortal dare to pretend that he is the Son of God?

For it does not seem likely to me that the remnants of diabolical fraud, now scarcely surviving in a very few people, will again grow strong against the Catholic law; and, although divine power is without limits, that the injury of the ancient serpent should be prolonged to this point, so that, after wars of unbelief have been extinguished for so many ages, he should disastrously revive them and once again raise his impious head, though cast down by the worship of the Church throughout every region of the earth—he who is so tormented by the invocation of the venerable majesty that he scarcely now dares approach even the dens of those criminals, while tortured by the hidden destruction of his fires, he trembles all around at whatever he hears bearing the name of the Catholic religion.

**ZACCHAEUS.**—You wish savage things to be recalled to memory, and the inescapable crushing of the human race to be brought forward through an account of the final events. These things must be spoken of with such mournful emphasis that, as it is written, “There have never been, nor will there ever be, such things” (Dan. XII, 1).

But human faithlessness and the immeasurable extent of sins will bring these things to pass. They are not decreed as though by some necessity, but foretold through foreknowledge, as Scripture declares concerning the Amorites: “The sins of the Amorites have not yet been completed” (Gen. XV, 16).

Daniel likewise, because the completion of sins was to come, establishes that the consummation would follow. Hence the Lord too, lamenting in the Gospel the corruption of the human race, says: “When the Son of Man comes, do you suppose that he will find faith on earth?” (Luke XVIII, 8).

The Apostle also, rebuking the wickedness of those times, says: “In the last days there will be perilous times. People will be lovers of themselves, blasphemers, proud, disobedient to parents, senseless, disorderly, without affection, without mercy” (II Tim. III, 2–3). Although they knew the righteousness of God (Rom. I, 32)—that is, the future judgment—they did not understand it, because those who do such things are worthy of death.

It is therefore a matter of certain belief that the Antichrist will come—indeed, that the devil will rage under the appearance of a man. Yet he will condemn paganism and encourage circumcision. For the Son of God could not otherwise be believed unless he falsely asserted that the restoration of the ancient law had been manifested by himself; and first he will subject to himself the Jews, the very head and source of all faithlessness and deceit. For they know that Christ will come and confess him to be the eternal Judge; but, in order to excuse the atrocity of the crime they committed, they do not believe that he came in the body which they killed.

[Note: [Col. 1159D] In the printed editions, *possit* (“could”), incorrectly. Below, where we printed *Deum se quidem* (“that he was indeed God”), the reading was *Deum esse quidem* (“that he was indeed God”); and where we printed *perditionis suae* (“of his destruction”), the reading was *perditioni suae* (“for his destruction”).]

To the heretics, however, that predicted pretender will assert that he is God, though lesser than the Father, so that, finally taking their impiety upon himself for his own destruction, he may mingle it with his own; and in both groups that saying from the Gospels may be fulfilled: “They will believe in iniquity,” he says, “who were unwilling to believe the truth” (Rom. 2:8).

Then he will capture the Gentiles, as though they were beasts deprived of rational understanding, by the marvels of his fantasies, so that, when nearly all the nations have been ensnared, even the elect, if it can be done, may be led astray by such deceits; and the multitude will give authority to this evil. From there he will introduce the ancient error of wickedness; and he who will first tear down the traces of idols will order statues to be set up for himself in holy places, and by compelling them with terrible force to worship these, he will subtly strive to restore what he had pretended to hate.

For, as I have said, against those ignorant of such a crime he will employ signs, and against those fickle of purpose, rewards; while he will constrain the holy by punishments to venerate with submissive worship the images of the accursed abomination and death-dealing countenances. Nowhere will those fleeing find a secure retreat, nor any hidden place in which to conceal themselves, since those in hiding will be betrayed by their nearest companions, and those fleeing will be consumed by starvation. For the Lord, speaking in the Gospel about his evils, says: “Then one person will betray his neighbor” (Matt. 24:10).

That the faithful will have to be killed by want, the Apocalypse declares as follows: “He will cause all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves, to give themselves marks on their right hand or on their foreheads, so that no one may be able to buy or sell except one who has the mark or the name of the beast” (Apoc. 12:16–17).

[Note: [Col. 1160D] The Vindobonensis manuscript reads, “that each person may give himself [a mark].” Not far below, the Lemovicensis codex has “whom … will come”; the earlier edition, “than … will come” [feminine]. Below, the Vindobonensis reads, “and the wonderful one will corrupt many and will direct [them].”]

Daniel foretold that he would come in these words: “A wicked king will arise, with a bold face and understanding of propositions; his power will be strong. He will corrupt and direct marvelous things, and will destroy the strong and the holy people. Deceit will be in his hand, and he will magnify himself in his heart; abundance will corrupt many, and he will stand for the destruction of many.” And again: “The king will exalt himself against every strong one and will magnify himself above every god. He will speak proud things and will prosper until wrath is completed; for at the consummation it will come to pass, and he will not understand the God of his fathers, and he will not turn to the desire of women” (Dan. 11:36–37).

[Note: [Col. 1161D] The Vindobonensis has *enim finem* (“for the end”) and *in omnem* (“and in every”). Below it reads “presenting himself as pure”; the printed editions have “he might present,” undoubtedly incorrectly.]

Thus you understand that the king of that accursed time must be considered above all others: those whom he cannot corrupt by force and fraud he will strive to seize by enticement. Not understanding the gods of his fathers—that is, the pagan gods—he will display, in an enervated body, chastity as though he were pure, and he will ravage the holy people, that is, the Christian people, by cruel slaughter.

But the marks of heavenly wrath will follow this grief of the world and the tribulation of the righteous; and, before the great day of the Lord arrives, the pain of unspeakable evils will precede the end of all things, while, before the final dissolution of the world, the remnants of the human race will either have to perish forever in sacrilege or, because of sacrilege, cease to live in this world.

## CHAPTER VIII. When he will come, or how long his kingdom will last

**APOLLONIUS.**—You have taught with great clarity and distinctness that the Antichrist will truly come and rage toward the destruction of the world and against the Catholic law. But the exposition begun has not yet reached when he will come or how long he will exist. Therefore, examine carefully what periods will enclose his reign and what signs will precede his coming. For if, amid such a multitude of signs and such power of his kingdom, spiritual wickedness displays its will, and if there will be no means either of destroying him or of exposing him more clearly, then, as I think, even the faithful themselves will have no opportunity to recognize the falsehood, and no kinds of remedies will save those who are in doubt, if the coercion of transgressions, full of ferocity and phantasms, is obscurely perceived. Therefore distinguish this part also, concerning doubtful matters, by an exposition of divine authority, so that, when the deceits have been torn up by the roots, the doubtful may be instructed and the weak strengthened, while the plots of the deceiver are exposed and the madness of the reveller is perhaps confined by the brevity of the time.

**ZACCHAEUS.**—The Antichrist will plainly come, but Christ will immediately follow. And although, as he himself says, neither the angels know the day or hour of his coming (Matt. 24:36), since the Father has reserved knowledge of this secret in his own power, nevertheless the same teacher has clearly set forth beforehand the signs by which, weighing the present condition of the time, we recognize that the final events are immediately at hand.

For he says: “When you see signs in the heavens and wonders on the earth, nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, battles and reports of battles, famine and earthquakes in various places, then these will be the beginnings of sorrows, but not yet the end” (ibid., 6, 8; Luke 21:10–11).

Now review each point, and understand from what is happening or has happened what remains. You will certainly see that only this is lacking which can be assigned or joined to the last things. For who lives, possessing the peace of his homeland, having been born? What people within their native land is accustomed to labor, or is restrained from inflicting or suffering danger either by concern for its own safety or by domestic affection?

The impious madness of war burns, and cruel insanity delights in weapons and plunder. From this source avarice’s gaping jaws are fed with blood, and when it has set everything ablaze with almost countless deaths, it nevertheless, thirsting for the survivors, either lays them low or strips them. Neither love preserves relatives, nor justice strangers. Meanwhile, groaning piety is banished and, driven from human minds, is compelled to remove the traces it had previously left.

Moreover, kingdoms clash with kingdoms, and they expel from the thrones of their rightful seats emperors unsuspected of such crimes. Add the unspeakable threats of prodigies, the exceedingly frequent earthquakes, and the many signs that have shone in the heavens. Why should I speak of the fatal outcomes of famine, and of the ravenous desires of those wasting away, filled with the unspeakable food of human bodies? The mind shudders to speak of famine fed by parricides, and of the remains of beloved bodies buried in the entrails of their own kind, so that they might perish more savagely than they had lived.

[Note: [Col. 1161D] The Vindobonensis reads “indeed to be present,” or “to exist.” Not far below, where “when everything will have succeeded” is read, the codex of St. Arnulf has “when everything will have been cut down.” Immediately we have written, from the Vindobonensis and Lemovicensis codices, “groaning meanwhile,” whereas the earlier edition read “groaning on the earth,” which gives no sense.]

Consider, I ask, whether this age can long endure what the human tongue scarcely dares to utter. Do these things rage in this way while the devil is at leisure? Although they must rightly be reckoned among our sins, they are nevertheless carried out by his concealed work—

[Note: [Col. 1162D] So the Vindobonensis; the earlier edition had “covered by his work,” incorrectly. Nor is the codex of St. Arnulf better, which reads “begun by his work.”]

—by him who is soon to engage in open conflict and who is now pressed by the extremities of the last things, so that he has already begun, by the desolation of the world, to do what the Gospels foretold must be fulfilled. For the Lord added these words to what has now been recalled: “When you see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place—let the reader understand” (Matt. 24:15); that is, when there will be universal desolation throughout the lands, when the abomination of accursed images is placed above the sacred altars, “and this gospel has been preached throughout the whole world, then the end will come” (ibid., 14).

What portion or habitation of the earth now exists that does not know the name of our religion—or rather, what place has not sent us members who believe from among its own people? Hence the preaching of the Gospel is understood to have been almost completed. Yet it will be completed in the speech of Elijah, who is now to come.

[Note: [Col. 1162D] “Then” seems to be the reading required.]

For he foretold that first the Antichrist and then Christ would be present for three and a half years each.

[Note: [Col. 1162D] In the printed editions, “may he preach,” with “whoever”; in the Vindobonensis, “he foretold”; in the same codex and in the Lemovicensis, “whoever,” rather than “whoever whatsoever.”]

Although the Apocalypse indicates that each will reign for an equal period, the Savior suggests in the Gospel that his days will nevertheless be shortened, lest the flesh, overcome by the duration of intolerable evils, succumb. For he says: “And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved” (ibid., 22).

This does not mean that the fixed arrangement of days and nights established from the beginning is to be changed, or that the intervals of the hours of passing time are to be cut short. Rather, just as the slaughter of the people announced through Nathan for three days obtained, by divine mercy, only three hours, so we believe that the reign of that accursed time is to be shortened not in duration but in number. The limit is to be imposed not upon the divine ordinance but upon the commands of the madman, so that, at the resurrection after the struggle of so great a conflict, both the devotion of the faithful and the faithlessness of the impious may be revealed, while the brief domination of the ancient enemy is driven away and the reverence due to the coming God is honored by the confessions of the saints.

## CHAPTER IX. In which Scriptures the resurrection has been promised

**APOLLONIUS.**—As it seems, and as I believe is evident to the minds of the anxious, the obscurity of the ambiguous proclamation has been dispelled, and knowledge of the final time has been brought wholly into the open—especially since, with the evils of these days confirming it, the reasoning is clear, and it is rightly believed that nothing remains except that the presence of the prophets who will announce these things should be demonstrated.

Now, when your questions have been completed, grant this one thing: teach that the resurrection, already believed possible through God’s power, has also been promised. Let not an assertion of such immense marvel reach us unsupported by the authority of heavenly decrees; rather, let what was intimated in the earlier books be strengthened by the instruction now given, bringing joy to believers and removing disputation from those who doubt, while they acknowledge both that it is possible through God’s power and that it will occur according to his promise.

**ZACCHAEUS.**—So abundant is the generosity of divine mercy toward human beings that God wished to prove, before accomplishing them, those things which earthly frailty scarcely believes, and to confirm believers by truths before proving them to those who would believe only after doubting.

For although he has inserted this part of his gift throughout nearly all the volumes of Scripture, he demonstrated it specially through Ezekiel, showing that human beings can more easily be raised by him than they were made, and that it is useless to mourn here as lost those whom no impossibility prevents from being restored.

For he says:

“And the spirit of the Lord took me, and behold, there was a plain, and it was full of bones. And he led me around among them in a circuit, and behold, they were exceedingly dry. And he said to me: ‘Son of man, will these bones live?’ And I said: ‘You know, Lord.’ And he said to me: ‘Prophesy over them, and say: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing sinews upon you and entrails, and I will cover you with skin, and I will give you spirit, and you will live.’

“And behold, bone came together with bone, and sinews and entrails grew upon them, and skin rose over them; but they lay without spirit. And he said to me: ‘Prophesy, son of man, to the spirit, and say: Thus says the Lord to the spirit: Come, spirit, from the four corners of heaven, and breathe upon these bones, and they will live.’

“And it happened: they stood upon their feet, a very great assembly. And he said to me: ‘Son of man, these bones are the house of Israel. They say: “Our hope is utterly vain; we have perished.” And they shall know that I am the Lord when I bring them out of their graves and make my people live, and place them in their own land, and do these things,’ says the Lord” (Ezek. 37:1–14).

Therefore the Savior said to the Sadducees, who did not believe in the resurrection: “How have you read, ‘The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’? He is certainly not the God of the dead but of the living” (Luke 20:38).

The Apostle also proclaimed a difference in merits under the comparison of the elements, saying: “One is the brightness of the sun, another the brightness of the moon, and another the brightness of the stars; for star differs from star in brightness. So also is the resurrection of the dead” (1 Cor. 15:41–42).

John likewise asserts that even those whom the sea covers with its waves will be restored, saying: “And the sea will give up its dead” (Rev. 20:13).

Then what David sang will be fulfilled: “God will come openly, and he will not be silent; fire will burn before him, and a mighty storm will surround him” (Ps. 49:3).

Hence Peter says in his Epistle: “What kind of people ought we to be, brothers, on that day, when the heavens will pass away with great force and the elements will be dissolved by fire?” (2 Pet. 3:6).

Then the words of the holy Apostle will be uttered: “Where is your sting, O death? Death has been swallowed up in your victory” (2 Cor. 15:55).

And those who now fill the paths of righteousness with tearful seeds, bringing back sheaves of precious death, will shine with the honor of lofty crowns. Of them it is written: “The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice upon their couches” (Ps. 149:5). And again: “They will exult like calves released from their bonds.”

[Note: [Col. 1163] So the Vindobonensis; the printed editions have “released from chains.”]

“And they will run like sparks among reeds” (Wis. 3:7).

These will be summoned by the words of the Lord, from the established seat of the heavenly throne: “Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world” (Matt. 25:34).

But the sentence pronounced against the impious will pursue them: “I was silent; shall I always be silent?” (Isa. 42:14). That is: “I am no longer subject, so that I can be crucified by those who deny me; rather, supported by the paternal majesty that you see, I—who had died from the weakness of the flesh but live by the power of God, presiding upon the throne of the eternal Judge—condemn my enemies by no other sentence than the one I foretold in the Gospels: ‘Go, accursed ones, into the eternal fire which my Father prepared for the devil and his angels’ (Matt. 25:41), where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth” (Matt. 8:13).

These are the matters which you may allow me to bring to your attention in my own voice. They must be avoided by the labor of mind and body, and those things prepared for the elect must be entered. Do not ask about their greatness or form, for it will be: “What eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart” (1 Cor. 2:9).

But if we either hear or see the incomparable pleasantness of certain regions and scents scarcely credible; if among some peoples rivers flow turbid with gold, and a gem serves in place of a stone; if cinnamon and amomum grow everywhere in abundance; if, finally, soft woods breathe fragrant frankincense and drip with precious balsams; if, even for us, under corruptible air, lilies painted with colors shine so brightly that they permit no imitation of themselves in any clothing or scent—what kind of beauty the riches of eternity will possess, what splendor the heavenly dignities will have, neither speech nor understanding can express.

Accept this much with certainty: nothing there will be necessary, nothing will be lacking; rather, God will generate for all people, through the immeasurable novelty of all joys, whatever is judged worthy of possessing his presence.

Now, I say, having been strengthened by the instruction I have been able to give, I continually warn you not to set down the plow of God’s cultivation and look back at what you have abandoned, or, while striving toward the prize you have set before you, slow the course of your eager purpose. Unless the contest has been completed, the palm does not follow; nor is the triumph of distinguished glory granted except after the contest has been brought to an end.

Hence Solomon says: “Praise is sung at the departure.” And in the Gospel: “Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved” (Matt. 10:22).

[Note: [Col. 1165C] The Vindobonensis reads this way; the earlier edition had “therefore by faith.” Below, we have written “of conscience” from the Lemovicensis and Vindobonensis codices, where “of steadfastness” had been read, a less suitable sense. Not far below, the Lemovicensis has “he will give, believe,” where the reading was “he will give to the believer.”]

Therefore let your faith be blessed, and always remember your instructor before God. Do not be excessively shaken by fear of the world or of the evils that threaten. God is the helper in all things; and when he supplies strength to the spirit, the flood of storms will run off into harmless foam, provided that the first weapons of an excellent conscience are not lacking.

And if the necessity of the announced tribulation comes, let firm confession withstand the enemy. He who promised that he would provide words will give the believer patience in sorrow; and the kindly one will bestow the aid of martyrdom, who warned us that we should defend the honor of his name even by death, saying: “Whoever loses his life for my sake will preserve it for eternal life” (Luke 9:24).

And again: “Whoever leaves wife, children, parents, and everything he has for my name’s sake will receive a hundredfold in this age, and in the future, in addition, eternal life” (Matt. 10:30).

Nevertheless, he permits those whom he knows to be tested for a little while, so that, having undergone the labor of the examination, they may please themselves, and so that justice may likewise reward the afflicted there, when he begins to judge their persecutors.

## CHAPTER X. Prayer to God

**APOLLONIUS.**—The order of the questions has been completed, and the vows expressed in the answers have been fulfilled. The fire of more devoted faith has been kindled by the testimony of the Scriptures as we have passed through them. You possess the ready fruit of your instruction, and, unless the weakness of the flesh prevents it, a spirit prepared to act.

[Note: [Col. 1165D] We have chosen to print this reading, whereas previously “may accomplish” had been read; and the healing hand was no less necessary than somewhat below, where the edition printed “he promised by giving himself.”]

May he provide the means to accomplish it—he who, by his gift, has permitted you to desire great things. For what is the point of exceptional care for the body, which will someday be reduced to dust? What benefit will soft sleep provide without the exercise of merits? What benefit will worldly honor, sought with great labor or at great price, provide, or the pleasantness of foods that will perish after passing the throat?

[Note: [Col. 1165D] The final two words have been added from the Vindobonensis, from which below also we have written “acceptance,” where “exception” had been read.]

There is no acceptance of persons there, nor will burdens of possessions follow the dead. Naked we entered this world; naked we must leave it. As David says: “The men of riches sleep, and they will find nothing in their hands” (Ps. 75:6).

And according to Solomon, many will have to say such things: “What did pride profit us? Or what did the boasting of riches bring us? All those things passed away like a shadow” (Wis. 5:8).

[Note: [Col. 1166C] The Vindobonensis also has this reading; the earlier edition had “the display of wealth.” Not far below: “when you have raised up,” or “when you have raised yourself”? Immediately we have written, from the Vindobonensis and Lemovicensis codices, “will be folded up,” where the edition had “will be presented.”]

Rather, Creator of all things, instruct the mind bound by your worship, and you who alone search the kidneys and the heart, complete what is desired, so that, when you raise yourself to shatter the earth, when heaven is folded up like a book and all things are dissolved in a terrible fire, the integrity of faith may be first in the one who prays, and no despair may confuse his conscience.

Then, under the sight of your majesty and of the innumerable multitude of angels standing before you, after the great honors of the patriarchs and the assemblies of shining prophets, after the lofty thrones of the apostles and the crowned armies of blessed martyrs, and likewise the happy bands of confessors and the companies of undefiled priests, may the throng that follows receive me, your servant; and may the labor of true perfection cleanse whatever stains this life may have.

But if you, generous giver of everlasting gifts, should consent to be merciful to a poor man, so that the proof of Catholic confession may also come through death, or so that what the weaker conduct of a slippery life perhaps cannot overcome may be sanctified by pure devotion of blood, then it will come to pass that, rejoicing forever in your gift, I may truly remember having sung in your praises:

“What shall I render to the Lord for all that he has rendered to me? I will receive the cup of salvation, and I will call upon the name of the Lord” (Ps. 115:12–13).

[Col. 1165]

# DISPUTATION BETWEEN THE CHRISTIAN THEOPHILUS AND SIMON THE JEW, BY EVAGRIUS

(From the Vindobonensis manuscript, Galland’s Library, vol. IX.) (C, S)

[Col. 1165D] There was, then, a disputation concerning the law between a certain Simon the Jew and Theophilus the Christian. The Jew therefore said:

“Cross-worshipper, standard-bearer, you profess yourself to be the author of the Christian law”—read: “teacher”—“and you have me as a patient listener, provided that you prove the truth through my questions, not by verbal enticements or arguments but by the presence of the law. If you defeat me today, make me a Christian; or, when I have overcome you, I will make you a Nazaraean Jew.”

[Note: [Col. 1167D] It seems that the reading should be: “a Jew from a Nazaraean.”]

**THEOPHILUS.**—Let not the hunchback boast as though he were upright.

**SIMON.**—Whom do you worship?

**THEOPHILUS.**—Certainly, if we speak and prove it boldly.

**SIMON.**—The voice of the sacred and venerable Deuteronomy resounds and says: “See that I am he, and there is no other God besides me” (Deut. 32:39). Isaiah also says: “I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no God” (Isa. 44:6).

**THEOPHILUS.**—It is the most sacred voice of Christ. If you wish to know it, you must first believe, and only then will you be able to understand. For Isaiah reproves you, saying: “Unless you believe, you will not understand” (Isa. 7:9, according to the Septuagint).

Therefore we know, acknowledge, and worship without doubt the invisible almighty God. Further, we profess Christ to be God and the Son of God. When he says, “I am the first and I am the last,” he signifies the two comings of Christ.

**SIMON.**—What of what he says: “Besides me there is no God”?

**THEOPHILUS.**—Christ God and the Son of God spoke this concerning himself, because he foresaw that the Antichrist would come. Of him the prophet Zechariah says: “Behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, and he will not visit what is failing; he will not seek the scattered; he will not save what is crushed; he will not complete what is sound; and he will eat the flesh of the chosen. He will overturn them. A sword is upon his arm and upon his right eye; his right eye will utterly dry up, and his right eye will be blinded” (Zech. 12:16).

[Note: [Col. 1167D] A word is missing. In the Vulgate edition it reads: “and he will break their hoofs.”]

Therefore Christ says: “I am the first and I am the last.”

**SIMON.**—Then you make two gods?

**THEOPHILUS.**—There is one God, from whom Christ is, and in whom God is. Thus Abraham saw three at the oak of Mamre—perhaps “Abraham”—and, running to meet them, greeted one, saying: “Lord, if I have found favor before you, receive water, and let your feet be washed, and refresh yourself beneath this tree” (Gen. 18:4).

This means that Abraham saw the presence of divinity, and that the tree of Christ’s cross supplied a shelter of refreshment to believers. Concerning this the prophet says in a psalm: “God stood in the assembly of gods; in the midst he judges the gods” (Ps. 81:1). Certainly he speaks of Christ, who taught and performed miracles in the assembly of gods.

Therefore in the forty-fourth psalm he says: “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions” (Ps. 44:7).

Which God did he call God, Jew? Certainly God the Father called Christ the Son of God. On his account and concerning him the most renowned of the prophets, Jeremiah, says: “This is God, and there is no other besides him; nor will he be reckoned apart from him. He found all wisdom and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved. After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings” (Baruch 3:36–38).

Again, in the forty-fifth psalm he says: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted on the earth” (Ps. 45:11). And in the sixty-seventh psalm: “Sing to the Lord, sing psalms to his name; make a way for him who rises over the sunset. The Lord is his name” (Ps. 67:5).

It would take too long to pursue further examples. The truth is proved by these few.

**SIMON.**—Quite properly you join the testimonies to those who worship, confessing with one spirit and agreeing with your mouth. But I want you to explain whether anywhere God established Christ as God by himself. Only then will I consider Christ to be God and the Son of God.

**THEOPHILUS.**—Unbelieving Jew, are you now disputing even from the prophets? Nevertheless, receive an answer to your questions.

God speaks to Moses, saying: “Behold, I have given you as a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet” (Exod. 7:1). Understand now that Moses was a type of Christ and was made the god of unbelieving nations. How much more is Christ the God of believers!

For just as Moses freed the people from Egypt and from Pharaoh’s harshest slavery, so Christ freed believers from the power of the devil.

**SIMON.**—If Christ is therefore God and the Son of God, how is it written in Genesis: “In the beginning God made heaven and earth” (Gen. 1:1)? He could have said: “In the beginning the Father and the Son of God made heaven and earth.”

**THEOPHILUS.**—You are mistaken, Jew, and you will never find the truth unless you understand the origin of truth. For if you are willing to believe, you will also be able to find who Christ the Son of God is in that beginning.

For it says: “God made heaven and earth”—that is, in Christ’s judgment, according to his will, and in whose image he deigned to make the human being. For he says: “Let us make the human being according to the image and likeness of God; male and female he made them” (Gen. 1:26–27).

**SIMON.**—He could have said this to the angels as well.

**THEOPHILUS.**—You are mistaken, Jew. To which of the angels did God ever say: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you” (Heb. 1:5)? And again in the psalm he says: “I will make him firstborn, exalted above the kings of the earth” (Ps. 88:28).

But to the angels he commands that they worship Christ. And again, in the Song of Deuteronomy, he says: “Rejoice, nations, with him, and let all the angels of God worship him” (Deut. 32:43, according to the Septuagint).

**SIMON.**—Prove to me that Christ is the commander.

**THEOPHILUS.**—I have already said so. Now receive another proof, if you can believe even in this way. When Jesus son of Nave was standing beyond the Jordan, he saw a man standing, with a sword sharpened on both sides in his hand. Jesus said to him: “Are you one of us or one of our adversaries?” He replied: “I am the commander of the army of the majesty of the Lord” (Josh. 5:14).

**SIMON.**—I also want you to explain to me how Christ is the Son, since all the saints too are called sons of God. Therefore, just as you proved to me that he is the commander, now prove that he is the Son of God, born from God. For divinity is very far removed from human intercourse and does not mingle with an embrace.

**THEOPHILUS.**—You speak like a Jew. Christ is God, God’s Son, the firstborn, brought forth by the word, uttered by the mouth. For just as, when God in the beginning had made the human being from the clay of the earth, he breathed his breath into him, and the human being became a living soul, so he begot his Word—that is, Christ—from the womb of his heart.

As it says in the second book of *Basilion*: “And the word of the Lord came to Nathan the prophet, saying: ‘Go and say to my servant David: You will not build me a house in which to dwell; but when your days have been fulfilled, I will raise up your seed after you. He will build a house for my name, and I will establish his throne forever. I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me; and he and his house will obtain faith’” (2 Sam. 7:4–5, 12–13, 16).

And in the second psalm he says: “Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on empty things?” (Ps. 2:1). Again, in the forty-fourth psalm: “My heart has uttered a good word; I speak my works to the king” (Ps. 44:2).

Isaiah says: “I heard of things completed and shortened, because God makes a shortened Word throughout the whole earth” (Isa. 10:22). This is the Word who healed our wounds. Of him the one-hundred-and-fifth psalm says: “He sent his Word and healed them” (Ps. 105:20).

Again, in another psalm the prophet bears witness, saying that God made the heavens mentioned above through Christ, who is the Word of God: “By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their power” (Ps. 32:6).

This is the Word who swiftly traverses the world and turns the souls of those who wander back to God through the new law. Of him the one-hundred-and-forty-sixth psalm says: “He sends his Word to the earth; his speech runs swiftly” (Ps. 147:15).

And Isaiah says: “Behold, the Word of the Lord became a curse for them, and they did not want it.”

[Note: [Col. 1169] Something seems to be missing here. Perhaps: “Would you not accept our prophet John? For the Jews do not receive the Scriptures of the New Testament.”]

For our prophet John, crying out with a prophetic mouth, says: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God, and the Word was with God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made” (John 1:1, 3).

And again the Son, by an equal kind of testimony, bears witness to the Father and attests the beginning of his own birth, saying through Solomon: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature. In heaven I caused an unfailing light to arise. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud” (Ecclus. 24:5–7).

You see, therefore, as your fathers were leaving Egypt, that it was Christ who went before them in the pillar of cloud.

Again, there in the Proverbs of the same author: “The Lord created me at the beginning of his ways, at the beginning, before his works; before he made the earth and before all the hills he begot me. When he prepared the heavens, I was with him; and when he marked out his throne, when he was making firm the foundations of the earth, I was with him, arranging everything. I was the one in whom he rejoiced; and daily I rejoiced before his face, when he rejoiced over the completed world” (Prov. 8:22, 30, according to the Septuagint).

[Note: [Col. 1169] The text reads *patraret* (“when he was doing”); read *pararet*, ἑτοίμαζε, “when he was preparing.”]

**SIMON.**—He may have said this concerning Wisdom.

**THEOPHILUS.**—You are mistaken, Jew, and your understanding is covered, as though by a veil—or perhaps “by the veil”—of ignorance. Not without reason did the most holy Moses cover his face with a veil, because that veil covers your hearts.

Approach therefore the Lord and the Son of God, and the covering of ignorance will be removed from your understanding. You think it was spoken of Wisdom, not knowing that Christ himself is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor. 1:24).

So completely did your kings, who reigned in succession, fail to receive wisdom and power except through the title of Christ’s name. I shall produce Daniel as the author of this claim, saying: “Vision and prophecy will be sealed. Everlasting righteousness will arise, and the Holy of Holies will be anointed. You shall know and understand from the issuing of the word in the answer; and I will build Jerusalem unto Christ, the Christ of your christs and the King of your kings. The anointing of Samaria will fail, that horn” (Dan. 9:24).

Then your kings were anointed, and all the prophets fell silent, because the one of whom they spoke had come, as Isaiah says: “I am the one who spoke, and I have come to proclaim good news to you” (Isa. 52:6).

Therefore, as we have said, he himself is the Christ of christs, the Lord of lords. I shall produce Isaiah as the author, saying: “Thus says the Lord to my Christ, my Lord, whose right hand he has held, so that nations may hear him: I will break the strength of kings; I will open doors before him, and cities will not be shut. I will open doors of bronze and break bars of iron, and I will give you hidden treasures” (Isa. 45:1).

Whose right hand did the Father hold, except that of Christ the Son, whom all the nations have heard, as the psalm says: “You have always held my right hand with me” (Ps. 72:24)? Or what city was shut to him? And to whom are all the bronze gates open?

Or would he dare to dispute about his birth, when the same prophet says: “The word of the Lord came to Ahaz: ‘Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, either in the depth below or in the height above.’ And Ahaz said: ‘I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord.’ And he said: ‘Hear now, house of David: It is not a small contest for you with human beings; therefore you will engage in conflict with human beings, because the Lord God will give you a sign. Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and his name will be called Emmanuel,’ which is interpreted, ‘God with us’” (Isa. 7:10–14).

**SIMON.**—I believe the prophets. Moreover, I accept Isaiah as highly authoritative; but I think he was speaking of another virgin. For when King Salmanassar of the Assyrians had sent his commander to Jerusalem to reproach the living God, Isaiah then prophesied against King Salmanassar, saying: “The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; she has shaken her head at you, daughter of Jerusalem” (Isa. 37:22). And when the angel struck one hundred and eighty thousand from the camp of the Assyrians, in this there was “God with us.”

TH.—You are mistaken, Jew; you have not yet removed your unbelief. If, then, you say that she was the daughter of Jerusalem, what son did she bear? Or who ate butter and honey? Or who was the child who, before he knew how to call his father or mother, seized the spoils of Samaria? Or what son did she rear from the seed of David? For Isaiah said:

“Behold, the Virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel. He shall eat butter and honey; before he knows how to call his father or mother, he shall receive the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria against the king of the Assyrians” (Isa. 7:14).

SIM.—Explain to me, then, how these things are to be understood, so that I may be able to believe; what is meant by honey or butter? [Col. 1171B] Or what spoils of Samaria did Christ receive?

TH.—If you remove your unbelief, you will hear the truth, lest what is written be fulfilled in you: “Like deaf adders that stop up their ears, which do not hear the voice of those who charm” (Ps. 57:5). For Isaiah boldly cries out against your unbelief, saying:

“The words of this book shall be for you like the words of a sealed book. If you give it to someone who knows letters to read, he will say, ‘I cannot read, for it is sealed.’ Or if you give it to someone who does not know letters and say, ‘Read,’ he will say, ‘I have not learned’” (Isa. 29:11–12).

First, Christ ate butter and honey in accordance with the infancy of all children. We believe this, and thus order our lives; and [we believe] that he was circumcised on the eighth day. Butter, however, is understood as the anointing of the Spirit; [Col. 1171C] honey as the sweetness of his teaching, which we attain. He took the spoils of Samaria in this way: while he was still an infant, he received gifts from the Magi—gold, frankincense, and myrrh; and afterward, when he had grown up and was teaching and revealing the whole truth, Samaria and Damascus believed rightly, abandoning their idols—that is, abandoning the Assyrian, namely the devil.

SIM.—You have indeed disclosed all the mysteries clearly. And since you have proved that Christ, the Son of God, was uttered by the mouth of God, begotten by the Word, [Note: [Col. 1171D] Perhaps, “begotten by the Father.”] and born of a Virgin, how then do you assert that he was born in the city of Bethlehem from the seed of David?

TH.—I shall produce Isaiah as my authority:

“A branch shall go forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root, and the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him” (Isa. 11:1).

For the branch was the Virgin Mary, who proceeded from the seed of David, and from her Christ, the flower of the patriarchs, was born according to the flesh. For the God who made the sign in Numbers by causing a she-donkey to speak wished to make a much greater sign, so that Christ would be born of a virgin. Or why would you and I be disputing unless the Virgin had given birth?

SIM.—I believe that a Virgin, as you say, could conceive by the Spirit. The question is whether a virgin could give birth.

TH.—Unbeliever! God could split a rock and bring forth water for the thirsty; [Note: [Col. 1171D] We think “people” should be added.] how much more could God command a virgin to bring forth a child! I shall give you yet another testimony, if indeed you believe Baruch, son of Neriah, who prophesied in Babylon.

SIM.—Do you therefore already consider me faithless, so that I would not accept Baruch, Jeremiah’s disciple, who, sent so many times by Jeremiah, addressed the people, and whom Jeremiah also ordered to write down his prophecy? And since Jeremiah knew that that people had been scattered into captivity, he prophesied; but he mentions nothing about Christ.

TH.—How, then, did he prophesy near the end of his book about Christ’s birth, the form of his garment, his passion, and his resurrection, saying: [Note: [Col. 1172D] These passages are not found today in the prophecy of Baruch.] “This is said to be my anointed one, my chosen one, hurled from an undefiled womb, born and having suffered”? And since his tunic was woven from above, as were all these things—Simon, if you believe, or when you come to the fullness of our Gospels, you will recognize that they have been fulfilled. But that he was born in Bethlehem, hear the prophet Micah saying:

“And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, you shall not be least, so as to be counted among the thousands of Judah. For from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose origin is from the beginning, from the days of eternity” (Mic. 5:2).

SIM.—We have indeed read many things, but we do not understand them in this way. Therefore I wish, concerning each matter I ask about, to learn what has been confirmed by the testimony of truth. Moreover, since God commanded circumcision, which he first handed down to the patriarchs—and you previously acknowledged that Christ possessed this circumcision—how then do you persuade me to believe you, when you prohibit circumcision?

TH.—We prohibit circumcising the flesh, but we gladly accept those who have been circumcised as believers. For Abraham, who became God’s friend and attained righteousness through faith before he was circumcised, did so not through circumcision (2 Chron. 20:7; Isa. 41:8; Jas. 5:23). For he says:

“I have appointed you father of many nations before God, because you believed” (Gen. 17:4).

Accordingly, he says:

“Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness” (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3).

He heard this before he was circumcised, and afterward received circumcision, showing that two peoples would come to the faith of Christ: one from circumcision and one from the foreskin. For if Christ had not been circumcised, how would you believe me today—or the prophets—that he would come from the seed of David? Circumcision is a sign of lineage, not of salvation.

SIM.—Then how was it that the angel strangled the son of Moses while he was still uncircumcised, unless Seffora, his mother, had circumcised him after taking up a stone? And when death threatened, she prayed, saying: “Let the blood of the child’s circumcision remain” (Exod. 4:23).

TH.—You are speaking against yourself, Jew; and earlier I told you that Moses [Note: [Col. 1172D] Read: “a type.”] was a type of Christ: everything he did anticipated Christ in figure. For Seffora, the woman who circumcised the boy, signifies the synagogue. As for the statement, “Let the blood of the child’s circumcision remain,” God says this to Moses:

“Build me an altar of unhewn stones, and you shall not apply iron to them” (Exod. 20:25);

that is, when Christ came, he was going to build the Church from an uncircumcised people.

SIM.—Prove to me that Christ circumcised no one.

TH.—Believe, and you will prove it to yourself. When you begin to read through the fullness of the Gospels, there you will find the apostle Matthew, the tax collector, and Zacchaeus, chief of the tax collectors, and many others [Note: [Col. 1173D] Here Evagrius considers the apostle Matthew to have been uncircumcised, that is, a Gentile rather than a Jew. Tertullian had preceded him in this opinion in his book *On Modesty*, chapter 9; Saint Jerome, writing to Damasus, marvels at this opinion and learnedly refutes it in these words: “As though Matthew too had not been a tax collector from the circumcision, and as though the one who, praying with the Pharisee in the temple, did not dare to raise his eyes toward heaven, had not also been a tax collector from Israel . . . . . or as though it could seem credible to anyone that a Gentile entered the temple, or that the Lord had a meal with Gentiles.”] who, though uncircumcised, believed with the Jews.

For if the sacrifices of the age—the offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs—were commanded to be offered, and the prohibitions have been removed, and the lesser people, that is, ours, was preferred to the greater, and the New Testament was set above the Old, so also he commanded that circumcision should now be celebrated not of the flesh but of the heart.

God says to Rebecca in Genesis:

“Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be divided from your womb; one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger” (Gen. 25:23).

And in Deuteronomy he says:

“You shall be the head among the nations, while the unbelieving people shall be the tail” (Deut. 28:44).

And when Jacob blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, changing the position of his hands and placing his right hand upon the younger, he was displaying the transformation of creation.

Concerning the final Testament Isaiah says:

“Behold, I make new things, which shall now arise, and I shall place rivers in the desert” (Isa. 43:19);

that is, the Gospels in the Church.

And Jeremiah says:

“Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will complete a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah—not like the covenant which I made with your fathers on the day when I led them out of the land of Egypt” (Jer. 11:7).

Now hear what Moses the lawgiver says about circumcision:

“In the last days the Lord will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring for the Lord your God, according to the commandment” (Deut. 30:6).

And Jeremiah says:

“Men of Judah and you who dwell in Jerusalem, renew your fallow ground for yourselves, and do not sow upon thorns. Circumcise yourselves to your God, and circumcise the foreskins of your hearts, lest wrath go forth and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it” (Jer. 4:3–4).

And God says to Jesus son of Nun:

“Make for yourself very sharp stone knives, and circumcise the children of Israel a second time” (Josh. 5:2).

Surely there was no lack of iron then? Rather, God was speaking to our Lord Jesus Christ, because through his apostles he would circumcise hearts spiritually; indeed, our apostle was called Simon and afterward received the name Peter.

SIM.—The things you have shown me are clear. But what can circumcision of the heart be, and what foreskin is to be circumcised from the heart?

[Col. 1174A] TH.—Every lust and desire is conceived in the heart. Therefore the circumcision of the New Testament is of the kind that God and Christ his Son revealed. Let us circumcise lust, greed, wickedness, covetousness, thefts, deceit, and fornications; and whatever you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another. This is the circumcision of Christians, which the first saints also possessed—namely Enoch, Noah, Job, and Melchizedek—who had circumcision not of the flesh but of the heart. God could have created Adam circumcised. [Note: [Col. 1174D] Lactantius says the same in the passage cited: “If God had wished, he could have formed man from the beginning without a foreskin.”]

SIM.—I am consumed by violent reflection that Christ endured such a cursed and shameful passion—if what you say is true, that our fathers fastened him to the cross. We know that Haman, deservedly cursed by our fathers, was hanged because he had sought the destruction of our race; when his death had been completed and the year had come around, we rejoice and celebrate the customary festivals of our vows, which we received as a tradition from our fathers. And we read that Absalom, who was a parricide and sought slaughter, was hanged on a tree. But if Christ endured this manner of death and hung upon a cross, why have we not received this very thing from our fathers, nor found him suffering it in our Scriptures, so that, as we rejoice over an enemy of our nation, we might rejoice over him? You will be able to blush, Theophilus, if you do not prove this statement at all. For it is written in Deuteronomy:

“Cursed is the man who hangs on a tree” (Deut. 21:23).

TH.—First understand the meaning of this statement. Recall the passage from Deuteronomy mentioned above, where Moses says:

“If someone has sinned and is punished with the sentence of death as an example, you shall hang him on a tree; and everyone who hangs on a tree shall be accursed” (ibid., 22).

But this is said of a sinner who has committed a mortal sin. Christ, however, committed no sin, as all the prophets testify; but he had to suffer so that Scripture might be fulfilled. For Isaiah says:

“He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth; but the Lord delivered him over for our sins” (Isa. 53:9).

For elsewhere we have shown that the prophet said:

“Behold, the word of the Lord became a curse to them, and they did not want it.”

And again he says:

“He was counted among the accursed” (ibid., 12).

Hear Jeremiah also saying in the Lamentation:

“The breath of our face, Christ the Lord, has been seized into the destruction of our nation; under his shadow we live among the nations” (Lam. 4:20).

We know that the most holy David, full of years, rested in peace and endured no passion of death or cross. Hear, therefore, Christ saying in the twenty-first psalm:

“They pierced my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones. They themselves looked and saw me; they divided my garments among themselves, and over my clothing they cast lots. But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me; look to my defense” (Ps. 21:17–20),

and the other things said in the three following verses.

Likewise through Isaiah:

“I spread out my hands toward a people that does not believe and contradicts, who walks in ways that are not good, but follows its sins” (Isa. 55:2).

Likewise in Jeremiah:

“Come, let us place wood in his bread, and let us wipe his life from the earth” (Jer. 11:19).

Likewise in Deuteronomy:

“Your life shall hang before your eyes, and you shall fear by day and by night, and you shall not believe in your life” (Deut. 28:66).

Likewise in the hundred-and-fortieth psalm:

“The lifting up of my hands is an evening sacrifice” (Ps. 140:2).

Likewise in Zechariah:

“And they shall look upon me whom they pierced” (Zech. 12:10).

Likewise in Psalm 87:

“I cried out to you, Lord, all day long; I stretched out my hands toward you” (Ps. 87:10).

Likewise in Numbers: [Note: [Col. 1175D] Read “not as a man,” as in Lactantius, *Institutes*, book 4, chapter 18, where he also cites this passage from Numbers, although I have been unable to find the passage in the book of Numbers.]

“[As printed:] Like a man God is suspended, nor does he, like a son of man, suffer threats.” [The note proposes: “God is not as a man.”]

And in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Church, he says:

“My brother is white and ruddy, pierced by the soldiers with a spear” (Song 5:10). [Note: [Col. 1175D] Read “who.”]

What else does this whiteness demonstrate except the faith of the people? For the redness signifies his passion.

For in this first coming of his, he was to endure every humiliation and deformity even unto death. Hear finally what he says in the twenty-first psalm:

“But I am a worm and not a man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people. All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads.”

And there also:

“My strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue clung to my jaws, and you brought me down into the dust of death” (Ps. 21:7–8, 16).

And there also:

“I shall please the Lord over a young bull, producing horns and hoofs” (Ps. 68:32).

What do you say, Jew? Was David horned? Come now, understand that cluster of grapes in Numbers (Num. 13:24), which two men carried back from the land of promise: this was certainly a figure of Christ hanging upon the tree. He came from the land of promise—that is, from Mary, who was of earthly descent. The carriers, bearing the pole, [Note: [Col. 1175D] *Phalanga*, or *palanga*, or *palangae*, are smooth poles used by porters for carrying loads.] displayed the figure of two peoples: one before, namely yours, turning its back on Christ; [Col. 1175D] the other behind, looking toward the cluster, namely our people.

SIM.—What will you say about the pomegranates that were brought to Moses together with that cluster?

TH.—The pomegranates most appropriately followed the cluster. They were clearly a figure of the Church, containing within itself a people marked by the redness of Christ’s blood.

SIM.—What will you say about the figs, or by what arguments and discussions of yours will you prove that the fig is not sin, when [Note: [Col. 1176D] The word “when” is superfluous.] Adam the first-created, in his transgression, covered his nakedness with fig leaves [Note: [Col. 1176D] Read “with leaves.”], which signified the itching and bitterness of sin?

TH.—You understand only the outer skin, Jew. For the fig tree and its covering of leaves [Note: [Col. 1176D] Read “of leaves.”] signify the figure of the old man. But if you wished to consider the spiritual man, that is, the inner man, you would find that the fruit of the fig trees brought to Moses from the land of promise has a spiritual meaning, just as King Hezekiah of Judah, after his life had been prolonged, received a cake of figs for the healing of his flesh. He added these words:

“Take a cake of figs and apply it as a poultice, and you shall be healed” (2 Kings 20:7);

that is, once your impieties have been crushed, you may recover the health of your desire.

Let us now return to the humility of Christ and his coming, about which we were speaking. You will hear Isaiah say:

“Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We announced him as a child: he had no appearance or beauty; and we saw him, and he had neither appearance nor beauty. He was a man placed in a wound, and one who knew how to endure weakness; for his face was opposed, dishonored, and not esteemed. He himself bore our sins, and for us he is in sorrows. He was led like a sheep to slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. And who shall recount his birth? For his life shall be taken from the earth. He was led to death by the wicked of my people; and I gave the rich for his death, because he committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth. But the Lord willed to deliver him over for our sins, and he was counted among the wicked” (Isa. 53:1ff., according to the Septuagint).

And there he likewise testifies concerning the humility of his first coming, saying:

“I gave my back to whips, and my cheeks to blows; I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting, and the Lord became my helper” (Isa. 50:6–7).

And Jeremiah says:

“I was like a sheep led to sacrifice, and I did not know” (Jer. 11:19).

Concerning this lamb Moses celebrated the Passover in Egypt as a figure of Christ, for the people of God could not otherwise be freed from the house of slavery and from Pharaoh’s oppression unless the lamb were slain, the Passover celebrated, and the doorposts of the houses marked with its blood, so that when the destroying angel came, they would be saved in the houses when he saw the lamb’s blood. [Note: [Col. 1176D] Read “when he saw the blood of the lamb.”] [Col. 1176D] This sacrament was fulfilled before the foretold coming of Christ. For this reason he was slain at his first coming, so that he might free us from the power of the devil and from the worship of idols.

He is called a year-old lamb because, after he was baptized in the Jordan, he preached for a year and then suffered. [Note: [Col. 1176D] The same opinion was followed among the Latins by Tertullian in his book *Against the Jews* and by Lactantius in book 4 of the *Institutes*. No one, so far as I know, after the fourth century, except perhaps Orosius, held this view. From this you may infer the antiquity of the writer.]

And we are regarded as marked on the forehead with his blood, so that at the second coming, when the devastation of this world arrives, we may be saved.

I shall give the prophet Ezekiel as the authority for this, for he too signifies the two comings of Christ, saying:

“Pass through the midst of Jerusalem, and place a sign upon the foreheads of the men who grieve and groan over the iniquity that is done in the land” (Ezek. 9:4).

And again he signifies the devastation of those who are not marked, saying:

“Go into the city, and do not spare the old man, or the young man, or the women, or the little children; do not spare them with the sword. But those upon whom you find the sign, do not touch; and do not spare my holy ones” (ibid., 5–6).

This sign was displayed by Rahab the prostitute, who was a figure of the Church, when she hung scarlet and broom-fiber [Note: [Col. 1178D] *Spartum*, a kind of plant which some Latins interpret as *genista*, broom.] in the window, so that when Jesus son of Nun came to conquer Jericho, Rahab and those who were in her house would be saved upon seeing the scarlet sign.

So also at Christ’s coming, when Christ the Son of God begins to come to burn this world with fire, the Church and those within it who have been marked on the forehead will be saved.

Thus Hosea (Hos. 1:2), who bore the type of Christ, is commanded to take a prostitute for a wife—that is, the Church, whom Christ took from the prostitution of idols, because the beginning of prostitution is the service of idols.

SIM.—Then is the Church a prostitute?

TH.—What else does “prostitute” mean except that she refuses the profit of faith to none of all who come to her? For after rejecting the synagogue, Christ took the Church for himself. Hear Jeremiah saying:

“I dismissed your mother and gave her a bill of divorce; I gave your mother that bill because I dismissed her” (Jer. 3:8).

And another prophet says:

“Bring charges against your mother, because I am not her husband” (Hos. 2:2). [Col. 1177C]

This is also the power of God, Christ, concerning whom Solomon prophesied in the person of the Jews, saying:

“Let us surround the righteous man, because he is opposed to our works. He reproaches us for our sins and for our discipline. He calls himself the Son of God. Let us see whether his words are true. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death. For there will be regard because of our words, or his. For if he is truly the Son of God, he will receive him from the hand of his enemies.”

They thought these things, and they were deceived; their wickedness blinded them, and they did not know the mysteries of God (Wis. 2:12–13, 17–18, 20–22).

And Moses says in Deuteronomy:

“You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous” (Exod. 23:7).

Scripture also testifies that he rose from the dead, saying in the psalm:

“For you will not abandon my soul in the underworld, nor will you permit your holy one to see corruption. You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence” (Ps. 15:10–11).

Likewise in Psalm 29:

“Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld” (Ps. 29:4).

Likewise the psalm says:

“I slept and took my sleep; I arose because the Lord will receive me” (Ps. 3:6).

And Hosea:

“He will revive us after two days, and on the third day he will raise us up” (Hos. 6:3).

And in Exodus the Lord says to Moses:

“Go down and testify to the people, and purify them, so that they may wash their garments and be ready for the third day” (Exod. 19:21).

And Isaiah:

“Now I shall arise, says the Lord; now I shall be glorified; now you shall see; now you shall be ashamed. The fear of your hope shall be empty; fire shall consume you.”

And concerning his death:

“The sun shall set at midday, and the day of light shall be darkened, and I shall turn your festivals into mourning” (Amos 8:9).

And Jeremiah says:

“She died while it was still day” (Jer. 15:9).

That he ascended into heaven David testifies in Psalm 66:

“Make a way for him who ascends above the west; the Lord is his name” (Ps. 66:5).

Likewise in Psalm 46:

“God ascended with a shout of joy; the Lord with the sound of a trumpet” (ibid., 6).

Likewise in Psalm 18:

“His going forth is from the highest heaven, and no one is hidden from his heat” (Ps. 18:7).

Likewise in Psalm 24, when Christ ascended into heaven, this was said to the angelic gatekeepers:

“Lift up your gates, princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter” (Ps. 24:7–8, 10).

But those who did not know that Christ the Word had entered into the Virgin, wondering that he should ascend into heaven in such a form and carrying back a victorious trophy, [Note: [Col. 1178D] Perhaps, “sword.”] ask:

“Who is this King of glory?”

They are answered:

“The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory.”

Likewise in Psalm 109:

“The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool” (Ps. 109:1).

Concerning the splendor of his kingdom at his second coming, Daniel says:

“I saw in a night vision, and behold, one like a son of man coming in the clouds of heaven. He came as far as the Ancient of Days. And royal authority was given to him; every glory shall serve him; his faith is eternal, it shall not be moved, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed” (Dan. 7:13–14).

“Say among the nations: The Lord has reigned from the tree” (Ps. 95:10).

Likewise in Isaiah:

“A child is born to us, whose rule is upon his shoulder; and his name shall be called the Angel of Great Counsel” (Isa. 9:6).

And if you should wish to know the complete fullness of the Gospels, you will find in our John, as Christ went to his passion, that he carried the cross upon his shoulders; this is what Isaiah says.

SIM.—You have shown me, with evident proof from my Scriptures, that everything was prefigured in Christ [Note: [Col. 1178D] That is, in the Scriptures or through my Scriptures.]; and I would indeed have wished to believe, if the interpretation of this psalm did not hold me back. For this psalm is said in Solomon: “O God, give your judgment” (Ps. 71:2), which you proposed to me earlier. Indeed, its title refutes you, since it says: “A psalm in Solomon.”

TH.—That envier who deceived the first-created man and deceived your people, through whose envy death entered the world—he has evidently taken possession of this thought of your heart, so that, [reading uncertain: *errollus*], you do not understand a matter made manifest and placed in the light. Solomon reigned in Judea for forty years, from Dan to Beersheba; afterward he sinned, as it is said in the third book of the *Basilion*:

“Solomon did evil and did not walk in the way of David his father, but built a high place for Chamos, the idols of Moab, and for their king the idols of the sons of Ammon and Astarte, the abominable idols of the Sidonians; and God stirred up Satan against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite” (1 Kings 11:6–7, 14). [Col. 1179A]

But Christ’s kingdom extends throughout the whole world. Therefore the prophet recalls him, saying:

“He shall remain with the sun and before the moon for ages, and he shall rule from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth” (Ps. 71:5, 8).

He is not speaking of Solomon, whose kingdom and years I showed you above.

SIM.—As I see it, the enemy of my fathers, the devil who blinded my mind, is withdrawing from my thoughts. I have begun to recognize the light of truth.

TH.—Believe, then; enlightened, begin to come out from the bonds of darkness. For Isaiah says this about Christ:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; therefore he has anointed me. He has sent me to announce good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to lead out those bound in chains and from the prison house, to open the eyes of the blind” (Isa. 61:1).

What else can this mean except the people of this world, held fast by the blindness of ignorance and bound by the chains of the devil?

SIM.—You have revealed many things, and things previously unheard by me; but there is still a scruple of distrust in my soul, because you observe everything with religious scruple. Yet you neglect the sabbath, which God commanded to be observed and kept. Moreover, you consume foods and wine in the manner of the Gentiles, although God specifically commanded which things from animals and fish should be eaten, which should be avoided, and that their carcasses should not be touched. Unless you prove this through the Scriptures, I am in danger of refusing to believe.

[Col. 1179C] TH.—I have already said above that the devil envies you because you are the son of your fathers, who, supported by so many benefits and freed from Egypt, stood around the shores of the Red Sea in a manner compared to bronze [the text is corrupt]. [Note: [Col. 1179D] This passage is mutilated and corrupt; it might perhaps be restored as: “At the sound of the bronze trumpet they surrounded the shores of the Red Sea.” See Exod. 14:31; 15:20.] Though supplied with abundant provisions and filled with heavenly manna, they passed into forgetfulness and dared to demand profane gods to worship. Jeremiah rightly said of you:

“If the Ethiopian changes his color and the leopard his spots, so too may you” (Jer. 13:23).

Evil sabbaths having been taught, that is, an imaginary rest of the seventh day was handed down. First, when Jesus son of Nun was attacking Jericho, armed warriors bearing the ark of the covenant went around the walls for seven successive days; on the seventh day they went around them seven times. The truth is evident: either they began on the sabbath, or, on the sabbath, when the walls fell, they conquered Jericho.

Moreover, God rejects the human sabbath, as Isaiah says:

“Your fast, your feast day, and your sabbaths my soul hates. You have become a weariness to me; I will not forgive your sins” (Isa. 1:13).

But God desires that sabbath in which you rest from evil works, so that in the thousandth year, which is the sabbath of sabbaths, you may be found free from evil works. These shall be the holy things to be kept [Note: [Col. 1180D] Read “in which.”] in which God delights.

As for the food you are uncertain whether you ought to eat, you are forbidden to admit not pork, but the deeds of pigs. Similarly, you mix water with clay as a pleasure; you join your sister to yourself in intercourse; you incite blood against blood; you search the earth through acts of plunder; you proclaim your festivals; you pray in the streets. Behold how you sin, and do not understand what is written about you in the psalm:

“They are filled with children, and they have left what remains to their little ones” (Ps. 17:14).

This is the sin of you and of your descendants.

As for fish, you eat those whose skin is clothed with scales; but the other things you pretend to avoid, drawn out in nets and mixed together in the multitude of fish, you eat thoroughly dried and sweetened in sauce.

But as for wine, show me through the Scriptures where drinking is prohibited, and where we are forbidden to eat your unleavened bread. You will hear the prophet saying:

“Their feet are swift to shed blood” (Ps. 13:3).

And again:

“Your hands are full of blood.”

And in Deuteronomy:

“Their vine is from the vine of Sodom, and their branch from Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall, and their cluster is bitterness. The wine of dragons is their wrath, and the wrath of asps is incurable” (Deut. 32:32–33).

If, Simon, you refuse to believe these many and great testimonies, you contradict your own salvation. Read, Simon, Daniel, and you will find the barbarian Nebuchadnezzar: he himself recognized the Son of God, whom you are slow to acknowledge.

“Did we not cast three men into the furnace? Behold, I see four men, and the appearance of the fourth is like the Son of God” (Dan. 3:91).

What do you say, Jew? Take care lest the denunciation of the prophet Habakkuk be fulfilled in you:

“Behold, you despisers, and look, and despair; for I am doing a work in your days which you will not believe if someone tells it to you” (Hab. 1:5).

SIM.—Bringer of salvation, Theophilus, good physician of the sick, I can delay no longer. Command me to be instructed in the faith and consecrated with the sign of Christ. For I think that through the laying on of your hands I shall receive the abolition of my sins [Note: [Col. 1180D] This passage should apparently be read: “For I think that through the laying on of your hands I shall receive the abolition of my sins.”]; indeed, just as Jacob blessed and, through the laying on of a hand, received [something—the text is unclear], so that the greater might come from the lesser, so Ephraim and Manasseh were enlarged through the laying on of hands.

Then Theophilus baptized Simon, and he attained faith. Simon began to give thanks to God, saying:

“I give thanks to you, Jesus, whom I did not see face to face; now, however, I believe in you with my spirit and my whole mind. I give thanks to you, Jesus, whom I did not hear; now, having heard, I call upon you—Jesus, whose knowledge I did not previously possess. Now I desire that my mind be in you, through whom I have come to know Theophilus, your disciple.

Lord Jesus Christ, if indeed I am worthy of your calling, strengthen me. For you show the way to those who wander, recall the lost, raise the dead, fasten unbelievers in your faith, and enlighten the eyes of the heart of the blind. [Col. 1181A]

You are the one who was with our fathers in the desert; you are the light of the lampstands; you are the altars and the bread of the Presence; you are the altar and the voluntary victim; you yourself are my life: pearl, crystal, silver yoke.

I ask you, Lord, do not remember the ignorance of my misery; for you are the one who bestows hidden benefits, and you have deigned to show me everything.

To you be honor, power, praise, and glory, here and throughout all ages of ages. Amen.”

[Col. 1181]

SENTENCES OF THE MONK EVAGRIUS

(Regular Codex of Lucas Holstenius, volume VI.) (S)

I. TO THE BROTHERS WHO LIVE IN MONASTERIES AND HOSPICES.

[Col. 1181B] Heirs of God, hear the sayings of God; and fellow heirs of Christ, receive the words of Christ, so that you may set them in the hearts of your sons; and teach them the words of the wise. A good father disciplines his sons; but a wicked father will destroy them. Faith is the beginning of charity; the end of love, however, is knowledge of God. The fear of the Lord will guard the soul; good self-restraint strengthens it. The endurance of a man produces hope; good hope will glorify him. Whoever subjects his flesh to servitude will be free from passions; but whoever nourishes it will suffer because of it. The spirit of fornication is in the bodies of the intemperate; the spirit of chastity, however, is in the minds of the abstinent. Withdrawal with charity purifies the heart; separation with hatred, however, disturbs it. Better is one thousand in charity than one alone with hatred in hidden places and caves.

Whoever binds the memory of evil in his soul is like one who hides fire in straw. Do not give your body much food, and you will not see evil phantasies in dreams; for just as water extinguishes a flame, so hunger extinguishes shameful phantasies. An angry man will be afraid; the gentle, however, will be fearless. A strong wind drives away clouds; the memory of evil, however, drives the mind away from knowledge. Whoever prays for his enemies is forgetful of evil; but whoever spares his tongue will not grieve his neighbor.

If your brother has provoked you, bring him into your house, and do not be reluctant to enter his; but eat your bread with him. By doing this, you will rescue your soul, and you will not have a stumbling block at the time of prayer.

[Col. 1181D] As charity rejoices in poverty, so hatred delights in riches. The rich man will not possess knowledge, and a camel will not enter through the eye of a needle; but none of these things is impossible with the Lord. Whoever loves money will not see knowledge; and whoever gathers it will be darkened. The Lord will dwell in the tents of the humble; but in the houses of the proud the curse will multiply. Whoever transgresses God’s law dishonors God; but whoever keeps it glorifies its maker.

If you imitate Christ, you will become blessed; but by his death your soul will die, and you will not contract wickedness from your flesh. Rather, your progress will be like the rising of a star, and your resurrection will shine like the sun. Woe to the wicked man on the day of death, and the unjust will perish in the evil time. For just as the raven flies away from its nest, so the unclean soul flies away from its body. Angels will lead the souls of the righteous; demons, however, will receive the souls of the wicked.

Wherever wickedness enters, there too is ignorance; but the hearts of the righteous will be filled with knowledge. The merciless monk will be poor; but whoever nourishes the poor will inherit treasures. Poverty with knowledge is better than riches with ignorance. The ornament of the head is a crown; the ornament of the heart, however, is the knowledge of God. Possess knowledge, not silver, and wisdom above many riches.

[Col. 1182B] The righteous will inherit the Lord; the holy, however, will be nourished by him. Whoever has mercy on the poor drives away wrath; and whoever feeds them will be filled with good things. In a gentle heart wisdom rests; the seat of freedom from passions is a soul that does good. The makers of evil will receive an evil reward; but the makers of good will be given a good reward. Whoever sets a snare will be caught in it; and whoever conceals it will perish by it.

A gentle layman is better than a furious and angry monk. Anger destroys knowledge; the long-suffering person, however, gathers it. As the south wind is violent upon the sea, so is fury in a man’s heart. Whoever prays frequently will escape temptations; but thoughts will trouble the heart of the negligent.

Do not take pleasure in wine, and do not let flesh entice you. Do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will depart from you. Do not say, “Today is a feast day, so let us drink wine; and tomorrow is Pentecost, so I will eat meat,” because for monks there is no festival on earth for filling their bellies.

[Col. 1182D] Christ’s Passover is passage away from wickedness; his Pentecost, however, is the resurrection of the soul. The Lord’s Pentecost is the raising up of charity; but whoever hates his brother falls into a great ruin. God’s festival is the forgetting of evils; but mourning seizes the one who retains wickedness. God’s festival is true knowledge; but whoever devotes himself to false knowledge will die shamefully.

Fasting with a pure heart is better than feasting in the uncleanness of the soul. Whoever destroys evil thoughts from his heart is like one who dashes little ones against a rock. The sleepy monk falls into evils; but whoever keeps watch will fly like a sparrow. Do not give yourself during vigils to useless stories, and do not cast away spiritual sayings, for the Lord examines your heart and does not declare you innocent of every evil.

Much sleep makes the heart dull; good vigils sharpen the mind. Much sleep brings on temptations; but whoever keeps watch escapes them. As fire melts wax, so good vigils melt evil thoughts. A sleeping man is better than a monk who keeps vigil in empty talk. The dream of angels gladdens the heart; the dream of demons, however, disturbs it.

[Col. 1183B] Repentance and humility raised up the soul; almsgiving and gentleness strengthened it. Always remember your father, and do not forget the eternal judgment, and there will be no offense in your soul.
